world.org_type: electricity distribution business (lines company) with 44 zone-substation power transformers

driver: A monitored signal that the standard reads as the unit's own fault can be carried in from an attached compartment whose ordinary operation produces it, so ranking units on the signal measured in the main body puts units with a leaking neighbour ahead of units with genuine internal faults; only attributing each unit's signal to its source, by its co-movement with the neighbour's operations and its composition, separates them.
driver_concrete: Acetylene in a transformer's main-tank oil reads as arcing and the fleet DGA standard codes it most severely; at two zone substations with in-oil arcing tap changers (Dunsandel T1 and Leeston T2) the barrier between the tap-changer compartment and the main tank weeps, so their main-tank acetylene rises with every tap change (r 0.998 and 0.995, twelve-month C2H2/H2 9.8 and 8.2) and their code-3 severities lead the fleet (9.64 and 8.07), while Southbridge T2, with a vacuum tap changer, carries the same acetylene (8.07) from a genuine internal arc; a slate built on main-tank codes spends two of its three outages on tap-changer seals.
stump: A competent solver codes every transformer under the fleet DGA standard from its main-tank samples (limits by preservation type and age, twelve-month rates, condition code 3 ranked by severity) and names Dunsandel T1 (9.64), Leeston T2 (8.07) and Southbridge T2 (8.07), two of which carry acetylene leaked from in-oil tap-changer compartments; the step that lands it there is reading main-tank acetylene as a main-tank fault, when its increments track each unit's tap-change counts and its ratio to hydrogen is the tap changer's, so the slate should take Southbridge T2 (vacuum tap changer), Rolleston T2 (4.98, internal arc behind an in-oil tap changer) and Coalgate T1 (4.73, thermal).

lineage.driver: The referral test is filed for each metered sub-unit against its own history, but the ready-made series sums the sub-units of an entity, and where an entity holds a second sub-unit carrying one seasonal load, a large fall on that sub-unit moves the entity total by a few per cent, inside ordinary variation, so screening the summed series ranks the candidates differently from screening each sub-unit and counting entities once.

notes: Re-root of task180 (architecture 2). Subdomain asset-condition-maintenance carried under Anomaly Detection & Diagnostics because DGA interpretation is fault diagnosis on condition-monitoring anomalies. Bespoke draw from how zone-substation transformers are built (in-oil arcing tap changers in a compartment sharing a barrier with the main tank on older units, vacuum tap changers on newer ones) and monitored (main-tank DGA on a schedule, compartment samples less often, tap-change counters on SCADA). No calibration corpus, no licensed wrong basis; the fleet DGA standard is filed in full and says nothing about compartment leakage.
layer1: laboratory DGA reports with sampling and analysis dates, below-detection values written as <n, O2 and N2 for the preservation type, corrected reports re-issued under the same sample ID, and a label oil temperature sometimes left blank
an asset register with rewind years, tap-changer types by make and model, and a last-service field not written back since March 2025
SCADA daily tap-change counters that roll over at 99,999 and restart at zero when a counter is replaced at a tap-changer service
a historian export of hourly top-oil temperature and load with UTC timestamps and no zone marker
a maintenance log in free text with tap-changer services, oil processing and breather changes
a mobile substation booking schedule for the 2027/28 outages
